title: Bulk operator recovery in an optimized ternary MERA: does recoverability of an inserted bulk leg track the causal cone or the minimal cut?
status: TESTED 2026-09-24 (SIM-2026-079): OUTCOME 4, SMOOTH -- the registered expected outcome. Level 2. Recovery onset in the optimized MERA (m_0.9 4.55) is indistinguishable from Haar-random networks (4.62); not cone, not cut. G5 not evaluable (chi 8 OOM). No geometric language per the kill conditions.
confidence: medium (chi 6 only; 8 seeds per arm; G1-G3 24/24)
origin: 2026-09-14 valuable-questions review, proposal P4 with P1's control folded in. Jon ruled 'both, recovery first' on 2026-09-18.
claim: For a reference R_low maximally entangled with the lower open end of a cut second-layer bond, the boundary region needed to recover it (m_half along the family A_m) is set by the minimal cut in the optimized critical-Ising MERA and not in a Haar-random network of the same graph. Only that outcome is a Level-4 candidate. The expected outcome is a smooth curve (Level 2, or Level 3 negative).
preregistration: research/tools/bulk-recovery/PREREGISTRATION-HYP033.md (design approved 2026-09-21, committed before tensor code; becomes final only after G0)
killer_test: Gauge-covariant by construction: f(A) = I(R_low:A)/2S(R_low), invariant under a unitary on the bond (gate G3, void if it fails). Cone-like m_half <= 2; cut-like 7 to 10; smooth w > 6. Cut-like in both MERA and C-HAAR is a graph property, Level 2.
counterfactual_novelty: Four outcomes genuinely possible. Honest prior: outcome 4 (smooth), then 3. Outcome 2 is unlikely.

design_findings_2026_09_21: v1 attached the reference to both open ends; the upper half is a state functional and v1's G1 would have failed. Fixed to R_low only. Graph count: cone and cut predictors differ by 8 sites at k=2, 2 sites at k=1; k=2 registered.
